title: fix(cron): prevent overlapping retries after execution timeouts
body:
Supersedes #137274, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.

Related: #137215.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes overlapping executions when a cron job times out but its original runner continues past the retry deadline.

## User Impact

Timeout retries remain enabled and wait for the original execution to settle. Late completion preserves the single recorded timeout outcome. No public API, configuration, or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker-owned finalizer now retains the active receipt while recording the timeout, then finishes only that receipt after the underlying execution settles. The scheduler owns the subsequent refresh, and startup recovery reuses the recorded outcome.

The older settlement module was removed by #169946, so this is an independent repair of the current owner. The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed.

## Evidence

- On main `028723cde2165962d8489b2548e74efaf18e6de3`, the initial fake-timer reproduction started the runner twice while the first execution remained held. The final one-shot and recurring regressions both fail on that unmodified main because the active receipt is prematurely released.
- With the repair: 102 tests across seven focused cron files passed (63.22s total command wall time). After the final scheduler-wake adjustment, all 40 affected tests in the watchdog, receipt-finalization, and worker-finalization files passed again (69.35s including compilation). The regressions preserve retry eligibility with rejected or stalled cleanup, fence execution until settlement, and retain one timeout plus one successful retry. Recovery coverage confirms no second accounting pass after restart.
- The initial CI found six TypeScript narrowing errors introduced by this repair. The correction makes the receipt required at the shared recovery operation; an explicit type check of the worker module passes, as do all 25 tests in the affected watchdog/recovery suites. The earlier local test-import graph did not reach that worker module. Changed-file lint, formatting, assertion-safety, max-lines and whitespace checks passed. The local test-line ratchet exceeded its 120s host budget; its exact-head CI check passed. The allocation records exactly 115 added regression lines.
- Fresh autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) found no actionable findings on the final staged tree `94b655267fb466152564e47e4407e291333cd26c`. A fresh P0–P3 review of the type correction also found no actionable findings. These were static reviews; runtime proof is recorded separately.
- Compatibility: no schema, stored format, migration, or status-enum change. Existing legacy-history recovery and receipt admission/retirement tests passed; the new restart regression preserves job settings and history while settling a recorded timeout. The advisory hosted review requests a latest-stable upgrade run; that operational proof was not run under this task's focused-test-only host constraint. The storage-boundary proof covers the changed lifecycle, with that limitation explicit.
- Candidate: `23805358a80b237f122c1452ed48c28744d6a1d6`. All required exact-head CI passed in [run 41213153484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41213153484), including production/test types, baseline ratchets, tests, lint, and security checks. Merged as `7caee827c5be71496b5f3ab8dcc6eee559b7db83`. No production Gateway or live state was modified.

<details>
<summary>Scope and tradeoff</summary>

Production net +43 lines; regression tests net +115; allocation +2. Removed obsolete host mixed-deferred batch splitting and unused finalizer options in the same owner, plus the superseded marker-retirement recovery fallback. The remaining growth carries execution settlement into the worker-owned receipt lifecycle and preserves accounting idempotency; the zero-growth target was not reached.

A runner that never settles keeps its own job fenced. Failed asynchronous receipt settlement logs a warning and leaves the receipt for startup recovery rather than admitting overlapping work.

</details>
